name: Driftclean Pressed Occasion Suit (Shelf Cut)
description:
A two-piece suit assembled from mismatched but color-matched salvage: jacket from one donor garment, trousers from another. The Driftclean Collective operates out of a Tier 1 basement laundry, doing alterations and suit-matching for people who need to look legitimate for legal proceedings, employment interviews, or family events. They've developed a practiced eye for pairing fabrics that read as a set under fluorescent light. The jacket is taken in with interior basting stitches that hold but won't survive aggressive movement. The trousers have a crease ironed so sharp it compensates for the slightly wrong shade of charcoal.

The Collective charges by the hour and by complexity. A basic match-and-press runs Φ8–Φ12. They keep a rack of assembled suits available for immediate loan or purchase. Regulars know to return the suit after the hearing — it goes back on the rack for the next person who needs it.
cultural_context: The Driftclean Collective is a known institution in its district. People give them donor garments voluntarily. There's no shame in wearing a Collective suit — it's understood as community infrastructure. A few Tier 2 labor organizers wear them deliberately as political statement.
story_hooks: The character borrows a Collective suit for a custody hearing. The jacket belonged to a man who died in a Crucible furnace accident — his name is written in faded marker on the interior lining. The character wins the hearing.
Someone is trying to shut down the Collective, citing 'unlicensed textile alteration' under a Corponation IP clause about donor garments. The Collective needs help.

A Vantablack analyst is running surveillance on a Tier 1 block and keeps seeing the same suit on different people at different legal events. It takes them three weeks to understand what they're looking at.
